Subject: Renewal: premium SLA & capacity increase request

Hi Evelyn —

We’re starting our renewal conversation for Skyline AI (contract to renew 2026-09-15) and want to explore upgrading to Redwood’s Premium Support and tighter latency SLOs. Over the last 6 months our 95th percentile tail is impacting a customer-facing feature; we expect a 2x token growth next quarter and would prefer a path to reserved capacity + premium response SLAs.

Can you share a rough sketch of the term/price delta for:
- Premium Support (24x7 oncall + 1hr P1 response)
- A latency 95th percentile target of <= 400ms for seq<=512
- Reserved capacity bump from 8→16 GPUs (or equivalent throughput) with burst capacity for seasonal traffic

Attaching our July usage export and procurement checklist to speed things up. We’re on a 12-month term today; open to extending if it improves economics.

Timing: would love a first pass by EOD Monday, and a short sync this week if you have availability.

Thanks —
Sara
Director of Platform Engineering
Skyline AI

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the context and the export — this is exactly what we need to kick off a concrete proposal. Quick responses below and a proposed plan: 

1) Premium Support: we can offer our Premium tier (24x7 oncall + 1hr P1) as an add-on.
2) Latency SLO: for seq<=512 we can target p95 <= 400ms with a dedicated routing + preferred instance class (will need to pin model variant / quantization profile)
3) Capacity: we can scope a reserved pool equivalent to 16 A100-GPU units; propose a staged ramp (8→12→16) over the first 90 days to reduce commit shock. Burst capacity available by contract.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll put together a term sheet (price deltas and staged ramp) by Monday EOD.
- Can we schedule a 30-min technical + procurement sync Tue 8/3 at 10am PT? Ben (CC) will join for the throughput sizing.
- If procurement needs a quick template, Marissa can attach a redline-friendly SLA addendum.

CC’ing Marissa for contracting and Ben for ops sizing.

Cheers,

Evelyn / Marissa / Sara —

Quick ops read: skyline’s July token profile shows heavy short-sequence loads (median seq ~220) but spikes in batch size causing KV cache pressure during bursts. To meet p95<=400ms for seq<=512 we should:
- Reserve preferred instance class (C5/optimized attention kernels) and pin a quantized 8-bit variant for production traffic.
- Add a dedicated prefix cache for top-10 prompt families (will reduce tail on repeated queries).
- Use a staged capacity ramp: 8→12 (day 0–30), 12→16 (day 30–90).

Operational notes: ramping in 30-day windows reduces wasted reserved hours and gives us time to tune kernel selection. If Skyline needs hard latency SLAs from day 1 we can offer an initial burst reservation for the first 2 weeks (chargeable).

Attaching a draft SLA addendum and a rough throughput table I used for cost estimates.

-ben
